D018_m001.question:
I’ve just been… off for the past nine months. Ever since that explosion on the night shift—I still see it when I close my eyes. I wasn’t supposed to be near the east wing, but I made the call to reroute a few guys last minute. One of them didn’t make it. I can’t stop thinking about it—like that moment replays in my head at random times, even during dinner with my wife.  

I used to take pride in running that floor, making sure everything ran smooth. Now, I can’t even get myself to walk the line most days. I don’t know, just feels pointless sometimes. I keep thinking, if I’d checked the valves myself or delayed the shift change… maybe he’d still be here.  

I’ve been on edge, too. My wife says I snap over nothing—a raised voice, someone touching my shoulder from behind, I jump like I’ve been shocked. Last week, a guy slapped my back in the break room and I nearly swung at him. I didn’t, but… I wanted to.  

And my memory’s not what it used to be. Keeps my wife worried—I’ll put my keys down and have no clue where. Probably not sleeping right, but I don’t want to close my eyes. When I do, I’m back there.
D018_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m002.question:
I’ve been struggling for almost nine months now—ever since that open house last winter. I was showing a vacant property late in the afternoon when someone came in unannounced, aggressive, shouting. I locked myself in a bedroom until police arrived, but… I can’t shake it. Even now, a slamming car door or a phone ringing too loud makes me jump—sometimes I flinch so hard I drop things.  

I keep replaying it: the sound of his voice, the way the front door burst open. These memories just crash into my mind, especially when I’m trying to relax. It’s like I’m back there. Because of that, I’ve stopped going to certain neighborhoods alone, and I’ve turned down listings. My clients don’t understand—some have moved on to other agents.  

I used to love dinner events, networking—now I cancel plans last minute. I don’t feel like being around people. Part of me thinks I should’ve canceled that showing, or at least taken more precautions. I should’ve known better. Now I just feel angry—constantly. At him, at the system, at myself.  

I’ve been forgetting things too—keys, appointments. Not like me. I tell myself it’s stress, but honestly? I feel like I’m unraveling.
D018_m002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m003.question:
I’ve been struggling for about nine months now—ever since that night during the late exhibit setup when the security system failed and I was attacked in the storage wing. Some nights, I’ll be brushing my teeth or turning off a light, and suddenly I’m back there—heart slamming, gloves torn, the smell of old paper and blood in the air. I can see the shadows moving the way they did, and for a few seconds, I don’t know where I am. It’s like I’m frozen, reliving it.

I used to love curating—the quiet precision, opening night receptions—but now nothing gives me joy. Even seeing a colleague happy over a new acquisition just feels… hollow. I keep thinking, *Why me? Why didn’t the director upgrade the cameras? Why did they leave me alone?* It wasn’t my fault, but sometimes I feel so ashamed, like I should’ve fought harder.

I can’t focus during team meetings, and if someone slams a drawer, I’ll jump so hard my hands shake for minutes. It takes forever to calm down. I sit there, palms damp, replaying it all. I live with it more than in my life.
D018_m003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m004.question:
I’ve been struggling pretty much every day for the past nine months—ever since that school lockdown. It wasn’t supposed to be real—just a drill—but when the fire alarm went off and the PA crackled, something snapped. I couldn’t move. My heart just started slamming in my chest, like I was back there—locked classroom door, the lights off, kids whispering, not knowing if someone was coming down the hall. Now I get this wave of dread just hearing certain sounds, even a loud laugh in the hallway.  

I don’t feel like myself. I used to love cooking for friends, going to games, even just a walk on a nice day. Nothing brings joy anymore. I keep asking myself what I could’ve done differently—even though I know it wasn’t my fault. But I can’t shake the guilt, like I should’ve protected them better. I blamed myself for weeks. Still do, some days.  

Making small choices feels impossible. I’ll stand in front of the fridge and can’t decide what to eat. Wear the same shirt three days in a row just to avoid picking. And if someone touches my shoulder from behind? I jump—like I’ve been shocked. My students don’t mean anything by it, but I can’t help it. I just want to feel normal again.
D018_m004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m005.question:
I’ve been feeling this way for about nine months, ever since that robbery at the bank. I was on the front line when it happened—the gun, the screaming, the way my hands wouldn’t stop shaking. I keep seeing it replay, like a movie I can’t turn off. Out of nowhere, I’ll be standing in line at the grocery store and suddenly I’m back there, heart racing, sweating. It’s exhausting.

Even when I’m safe, I feel like danger’s always just around the corner. I jump at loud noises—the door slamming, a phone ringing. When that happens, my chest tightens and I can’t seem to calm down for ages. My hands tremble, and it takes forever to breathe normally again. I’ve started forgetting simple things—where I put my keys, what I was just doing. I used to take pride in being sharp at work, but now I don’t even care. What’s the point? I’ve been passed over twice for promotion, but honestly, I can’t bring myself to be disappointed.

I don’t talk to my ex much, but I can’t help blaming him. He always said I should quit that job, and if he’d just supported me more or helped me find something else, maybe I wouldn’t have been there that day. I know it sounds unfair, but the anger keeps me from falling apart—almost.
D018_m005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018_m006.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—ever since that night last January when I was assaulted walking home from the lab. I used to be so focused, really proud of my work, but now I can’t even feel good about finishing experiments or presenting at meetings. It’s like something inside just shut down. 

I have these dreams—over and over—where I’m back on that street, except sometimes it’s not me, sometimes I’m watching it happen to someone else, but I still wake up shaking, heart racing like I’m running. It takes ages to calm down. If someone shuts a door too hard or calls my name suddenly, I feel like I’m going to jump out of my skin—and then I’ll snap. Last week I yelled at my labmate for moving my notebook. I felt awful after, but I couldn’t stop it.

I don’t talk about what happened. I avoid thinking about it. Sometimes it feels like there’s just… a blank spot. I remember pieces—the cold, the voice—but most of it? Gone. I don’t want to fill it in. I keep working, but I feel numb. Like I’m watching my life from far away. My advisor asked if I wanted to submit a paper for an award. I said yes, but when it got accepted, I just sat there. Nothing.
D018_m006.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m007.question:
I’ve been like this for just over a year now—ever since that armed robbery at the auction house. I was standing at the podium, mid-call, when they burst in. Nobody got killed, but one guy put a gun right in my face, yelling at me to open the safe. I… I can’t remember much of what happened during those few minutes. It’s like my mind just shut down. Whole chunk’s gone.

Since then, I can’t stand it when someone walks up behind me sudden-like—jumps a mile, heart pounding. One time, I knocked over a display table when my assistant came around the corner too fast. Broke a client’s antique vase. It wasn’t just the noise—it was the movement, the way he appeared outta nowhere.

I don’t talk about it. Not with my wife, not with the guys at work. If someone brings up the incident, I shut down or walk away. Sometimes I’ll wake up in a sweat, but I don’t remember dreaming.

I used to love closing a big sale—the energy, the crowd. Now, even when I nail a record bid, it feels… hollow. No pride. Nothing. My wife says I’m not the same man. She’s right. I don’t feel like me anymore.
D018_m007.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m008.question:
I’ve been working the night shift at a convenience store for about a year and a half now, and things haven’t been right since that robbery back in February. I remember the gun, the way my hands shook… but some parts? Like what happened right after he left—total blank. It’s weird. One minute I’m fine, next I’m sweating and my chest is tight just seeing someone in a hoodie, like it triggers something deep in my gut.

I stopped going to family barbecues, even though my mom always calls. I just can’t stand being around people. Feels like I can’t feel anything—not when my little nephew hugs me, not when my ex texts. Like my heart’s locked away.

I yelled at a customer last week for no real reason. Cursed him out because he tapped the counter too loud. I didn’t mean to—just snapped. My nerves are shot. If someone touches my shoulder from behind, I jump like I’ve been shocked. It ruins the shift. I’m tired all the time, but I can’t sleep without seeing that guy’s face.

It’s been over a year now, and it’s only gotten worse. I don’t even recognize myself anymore.
D018_m008.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m009.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—since my husband passed, but honestly, it’s like something inside me broke long before that. I used to care for others my whole life as a nurse, but now I can’t even care for myself properly. There are moments—just out of nowhere—where I’m back in that hospital room during Hurricane Katrina. I smell the damp, hear the screaming, feel the heat… I’m standing in my kitchen and suddenly I’m not there at all. My granddaughter says, “Grandma, you’re staring,” and I realize I don’t remember what happened for a minute or two.

I don’t like talking about that time. I can’t remember much of it anyway—whole chunks are just gone. It’s not that I don’t want to remember; I *can’t*. And ever since, I’ve felt… hollow. My daughter hugs me, and I just stand there. I love her, I know I do, but I can’t feel it.

Little things set me off—someone walks in fast from the side, and I jump like I’ve been shocked. I get angry so fast now, over nothing. One of the neighbors came by with casserole, and I snapped at her. Didn’t mean to—but I’m just… always on edge.
D018_m009.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m010.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—since the plant closed and I lost my job, but really… it’s more about what happened right before that. There was an incident—on the night shift. I don’t remember all of it, just pieces. Like the sound of alarms, someone yelling, and then… red lights flashing. But the middle? Nothing. It’s like my mind just ripped that part out.

Ever since, things have been off. Certain sounds—sirens, loud bangs—they hit me deep in my chest, like my heart’s being squeezed. I don’t go near the old industrial area anymore. Won’t drive that route. Even passing a warehouse with those rolling metal doors makes my skin crawl. I avoid anything that might trigger… whatever’s locked up in there.

My wife says I’ve changed. I don’t laugh like I used to. Feels like I’m just going through motions. I love her, but it’s like the warmth got turned off. Then there’s the anger—I snap at nothing. A coworker’s shadow moving fast behind me? I jump like I’ve been shot. I didn’t used to be this way. I can’t work, can’t sleep, can’t even be around people. It’s like I’m still trapped back in that place.
D018_m010.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018_m011.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time—this has been going on for over two years, honestly. It started after I was held at gunpoint during a robbery at the hotel where I work. Since then, certain sounds—like a door slamming or someone raising their voice near the front desk—just snap me right back to that moment. My chest tightens, and I can’t think straight. I don’t talk about it much; I just try not to think about it at all. When coworkers ask how I’m doing, I say “fine,” because opening that door in my head feels like inviting the panic all over again.

I used to believe people were mostly good, but now? I walk past strangers and assume the worst. Everyone seems like a threat. I blame the guy who pulled the trigger, sure, but also the manager for not installing better security. What kind of place lets that happen?

I’m always on edge—constantly scanning, never relaxing. My nerves feel raw. Little things—like a delayed shift change or someone being late—set me off. I snapped at a guest last week over a key card issue and almost got written up. I can’t keep living like this. It’s affecting everything.
D018_m011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m012.question:
I’ve been struggling for over two years now—since that night when the church was broken into, and I found the sanctuary vandalized. There was blood, graffiti… it felt like evil had taken over a place meant for healing. I keep having this dream—over and over—where I’m walking down the aisle, but the pews are empty, the cross is torn down, and I can’t move, can’t speak, like I’m paralyzed. I wake up sweating, heart pounding, like I’m still there.

Afterward, I started avoiding the church after hours. Even walking past it at night makes my chest tighten. I’ve stopped visiting members in the hospital—too many reminders. I used to believe people were basically good, that God had a plan… but now? I don’t know. The world feels like a ticking bomb. I should’ve been there earlier that night. Maybe I could’ve stopped it. Maybe if I hadn’t stayed late to counsel someone, or if I’d locked the side door… 

My wife says I’ve changed. I snap at little things—kids laughing too loud, a door slamming. She doesn’t understand; she tells me I’m not the man I used to be. I want to lead my congregation, but some days, I can’t even get out of bed. I feel like I’ve failed them. Failed myself.
D018_m012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m013.question:
I’ve been having these episodes for over two years now—started not long after a student brought a gun into my classroom. I wasn’t physically hurt, but I relive it like I’m back there. Sometimes I’ll be grading papers and suddenly I can hear the yelling, see the hallways emptying—my heart races, I freeze. It’s like I’m trapped in that moment, like I can’t get back to the present.  

After that, I started avoiding anything that reminded me of it. I switched schools, stopped going to staff meetings near the old building, even avoid talking to other teachers about school safety. Anything that brings it up just tears me apart.  

I don’t know if I believe in anything anymore. It feels like the world’s just waiting to hurt you. One bad decision, one second, and everything falls apart. I used to think I could protect my students, that schools were safe. Now? I blame the administration—the way they ignored warnings, dismissed concerns. They should’ve done more.  

And my temper… it’s like a wire’s always humming under my skin. A kid slams a locker, someone talks too loud—that’s all it takes. I snap. I’ve been short with colleagues, even walked out of class once. It’s affecting my work. I care about teaching, but I don’t know how much longer I can keep it together.
D018_m013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m014.question:
I’ve been struggling for over two years—since that incident on the night shift. A patient got hold of a scalpel during a code, and I was the closest. He came at me… I wasn’t hurt physically, but I can still see his face, the way his eyes looked. Sometimes, out of nowhere—like last week when a cart rolled down the hall too fast—I feel like I’m back there, heart slamming, the walls closing in. I freeze. I know it’s not real, but for a few seconds, I *can’t move.*  

I’ve stopped taking certain units, even though I love acute care. I won’t go near the East wing—too many memories. I turned down a promotion because it meant working with unstable admits again.  

It’s hard to trust people now. I keep thinking, *Anyone could snap.* My ex, he tried to come back, but I couldn’t—what if he’s hiding something? After everything, I feel like everyone’s dangerous. I blamed the physician who downgraded that patient’s status. He said he was “stable,” but *he* didn’t have to dodge a blade.  

And my temper—my coworkers walk on eggshells. I yelled at a nurse for misplacing a chart. It wasn’t her fault. But I just… erupted. I can’t keep doing this. I’m exhausted, but I can’t rest. I’m scared to sleep.
D018_m014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m015.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that night on duty two years ago—something I still can’t talk about without my chest tightening. I was patrolling the old warehouse when I interrupted a break-in. What happened after… I see it every time I close my eyes. Since then, if I hear a sudden noise or see a shadow move fast, my heart pounds like I’m back there. I’ve stopped going near that building, even turned down extra shifts in the area. Can’t help it—just being close makes me feel like I can’t breathe.

I don’t go out much anymore, not even with friends from work. They don’t understand why I won’t talk about it. Part of me feels broken, like I should’ve been stronger, faster—should’ve stopped it from going so wrong. I keep thinking I messed up, that I’m somehow to blame. My wife says it’s not my fault, but I can’t shake that weight.

And the anger—sometimes it just erupts. Yelled at my grandson the other day because he slammed a door. He looked so scared. That’s not me… but I can’t seem to control it. I’m not sleeping, always on edge. It’s tearing things apart at home.
D018_m015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m016.question:
I’ve been like this for over a year now—since the robbery at the store last winter. I was alone on shift when they came in, smashing things, shouting… one of them pinned me against the counter. It’s hard, even talking about it.  

Ever since, my nerves are just… always on edge. Even at home, with the locks double-checked, I can’t relax. I hear every little sound, jump at shadows. My manager asked me to handle the night audit again last month—it’s part of my job—but I couldn’t do it. Just the thought of being in the empty store brings back that same tight chest, the shaking. I turned it down and made up some excuse. Since then, I’ve avoided working late altogether. I’ll take any extra shifts during the day, but once it gets dark, I leave. No exceptions.  

There are certain customers, too—men in hoodies, especially—if they move too quickly, I feel my heart race, like I can’t breathe. I have to step away, find someone else to help them.  

And honestly? I keep thinking—if corporate had paid for better security, or hired security staff like we asked, maybe it wouldn’t have happened. They ignored the warnings. I wouldn’t be like this if they’d just listened.
D018_m016.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m017.question:
I’m a 36-year-old solar panel technician—I’ve been married for eight years, and up until about a year and a few months ago, I could handle just about anything up on those roofs, even the high ones. But since that day when the ladder gave way and my partner fell… I haven’t been the same. I see it over and over—his face, the sound, like it’s playing in my head no matter what I’m doing. I was right there, and I keep thinking I should’ve noticed the loose rung, that I could’ve stopped it. He survived, but I can’t forgive myself for missing it.  

Since then, I’ve started avoiding anything that reminds me—talking about it, even going near that site. Sometimes I make excuses not to go on certain jobs. At home, my wife says I’m distant, like I’m somewhere else. I don’t like talking about how I feel; it’s easier to just shut it out.  

But I can’t relax. Even when I’m off the clock, I’m always looking around—checking exits, watching for hazards. On the roof, I’m triple-checking every latch and rope, scanning the ground, the weather, everything. It’s like my body’s stuck in high alert, like the next thing could go wrong any second. And honestly? I feel like it’s my fault it happened at all. Like I failed.
D018_m017.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m018.question:
I’ve been having these nightmares for over a year now—sometimes I wake up sweating, heart racing, like I’m right back there. It’s always the same night, over and over. I was closing up the salon alone, and this man came in late, acting strange. I just wanted him to leave, but he… he wasn’t leaving. I can still hear his voice. Even now, when I’m doing someone’s nails—especially male clients—I get this tight feeling in my chest, like I can’t breathe right. I start staring at the door, watching every person who walks by, checking locks. I have to know where everyone is at all times.  

I try not to think about that night, but it just pops up—when I’m washing my hands, during music at work, even when it’s quiet. So I avoid talking about it, even with my friends. I don’t like being alone, but I hate feeling this on edge all the time.  

I keep thinking—if someone else had been there, or if the manager hadn’t made me close late, it wouldn’t have happened. It wasn’t my fault, but I feel like I should’ve done something. I just want to feel safe again, but it’s like my body’s always screaming that I’m not.
D018_m018.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m019.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—about a year and two months, actually—ever since the car accident. It wasn’t even my fault—a truck ran a red light and hit us head-on. My husband was in the passenger seat. He... he didn’t make it. Sometimes I still see it—the sound of the crash, his voice—just out of nowhere, even when I’m sitting at my desk trying to balance someone’s books. I’ll get this knot in my stomach, my heart races like I’m back there.

Since then, I haven’t driven. I can’t even sit in the passenger side of a car. I turned down a client meeting across town because it meant riding with my colleague. Anything that reminds me of that day—traffic sounds, the smell of gasoline—I avoid it. I used to love road trips. Now I barely leave the house on weekends.

I can’t explain it, but I keep thinking about the light. It was red. He had *no right* running it. That driver—he destroyed everything. If he’d just followed the rules, my husband would still be here.

And I’m always on edge. At work, I’ll flinch when the printer slams. I can’t relax, not really—not even at home. I check the locks three times before bed. It’s like I’m waiting for something bad to happen… again.
D018_m019.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m020.question:
I’ve been having these intense moments where I’m back there—on the highway, during the crash. It’s like everything else fades and I can smell the smoke, hear the metal crunching. Just last week, I was spotting a guy during a bench press and the bar slipped—no injury—but suddenly I was back in the car, heart exploding. It scared me, man.

It’s been over a year now, but I can’t seem to loosen up. Even at home, with music off, lights low, I’m still wired—like something’s coming. I avoid driving past the interchange where it happened, don’t go near cars if I can help it. I deleted all the rideshare apps off my phone. Can’t sit in the passenger seat without zoning out.

And honestly? I keep thinking about the driver who hit us. He wasn’t even drunk, just... distracted. Talking on his phone. I know it’s irrational, but I blame him for wrecking my confidence, like, my whole rhythm. Used to love moving fast, pushing limits with my clients. Now I hesitate. Don’t trust momentum. Don’t trust anyone watching their own damn screen instead of the road.
D018_m020.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m021.question:
I’ve been like this for about a year now—ever since that incident on the job when the gunfire broke out at the rally. I was right there, shielding the principal, but I can still hear the shots echoing in my head. Sometimes just a car backfiring makes my heart slam against my ribs, like I’m back in it all over again. My hands shake, I can’t breathe—no matter where I am, it hits hard.

I don’t feel much anymore. It’s like something inside shut off. My friends say I’ve gone cold. I don’t laugh like I used to. Nothing seems to matter. And the anger—I’m always on edge. Little things, like someone bumping into me or being late, and I want to snap. I don’t trust anyone, and I’m always watching the exits, always scanning the crowd, even when I’m off duty. 

It’s exhausting. I used to be good at my job—calm under pressure. Now I feel like I’m breaking down. I can’t sleep, I don’t connect with people, and I don’t know how much longer I can keep doing this.
D018_m021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m022.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—since the accident. I was driving home from visiting my mom when a truck ran the red light and hit me head-on. I don’t remember most of it, but I wake up from nightmares replaying the headlights coming at me, the sound of metal crushing.  

Ever since, everything feels… wrong. I can’t stand being in cars, even as a passenger. Just hearing a siren or seeing flashing lights on the road sends me into panic. I get this tightness in my chest, like I can’t breathe. My hands shake. It’s constant—like I’m always braced for something bad to happen again.  

I used to be close with my family, but now I can’t seem to feel anything when I’m around them. My girlfriend broke up with me because I “shut down” all the time. I care, I do—but I can’t show it. Inside, it’s just empty.  

And the anger—that’s the worst part. I broke my phone the other day just because it wouldn’t turn on. Last month, I got into a fight outside a convenience store over nothing. It wasn’t me, but I can’t stop it once it starts. I haven’t been able to keep a job because of it. I can’t even look for work most days—I just stay in my room, curtains closed. I feel broken.
D018_m022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m023.question:
I’ve been struggling for about 11 months now—ever since that night on the subway platform. I was just heading home after another late shift, and this man suddenly jumped in front of the train. I couldn’t move. I stood there, frozen, watching it happen. Lately, I’ll be at my desk doing a valuation or in a meeting, and suddenly I’m back there—the screech of the brakes, the look on his face—and I’m not in the boardroom anymore. It’s like I’m physically pulled out of the moment.  

The worst part is, nothing feels real anymore. I closed a $200M deal last month, but I didn’t feel anything. No pride, no relief—just numb. I used to live for that rush, proving myself. Now I wonder why I’m even here.  

I get angry, too. At nothing. At everyone. I snapped at an intern last week, screaming over a typo. I didn’t even recognize my own voice. Afterward, I just shut my door and sat in the dark. I haven’t told anyone. How do I explain that a single second—just one terrible second—ruined everything that came after? I can’t sleep. I can’t focus. And I can’t escape the feeling that I’m still standing on that platform, helpless.
D018_m023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m024.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—where I’m back in that convenience store, hearing the glass shatter, seeing the guy pull the gun. I wake up sweating, heart pounding like I’m still there. It’s been almost a year now.  

Since it happened, everything feels… muffled. I used to text my mom every day. Now, I don’t answer her calls for days. My ex kept saying I didn’t care anymore, but it’s not that—I just can’t *feel* anything. Not love, not sadness—just this heavy blankness, like someone turned down the lights inside me.  

And then, the anger just *pops*. Like last week, a customer got upset because their oat milk was cold, and I snapped—yelled at them to shut up. I know it wasn’t okay, but in the moment, I couldn’t stop it. Sounds scare me now. Loud noises, sudden movements—I jump, I get shaky. I quit my evening shifts because I can’t stand being there after dark.  

I thought I’d just “get over it,” but it’s like I’m stuck in that minute—the fear won’t leave. I don’t feel safe, even at home.
D018_m024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m025.question:

Since then, little things set me off—like the sound of screeching tires or even seeing a truck similar to the one in the crash. I’ll just freeze, my chest tightens, and I can’t breathe right. I used to love coming home to my husband—he’s been patient, but I can’t seem to feel that warmth anymore. It’s like something inside me shut down. I look at him, and I know I should feel love, but it’s gone. I snap at him for small things—like if he leaves his shoes in the doorway. Last week, I threw a coffee mug across the kitchen because he turned on the radio without asking. I don’t even know where the rage comes from.  

Work’s getting harder too. I used to be confident walking into clinics, but now I get nervous, distracted. I’ve missed follow-ups, and my numbers are dropping. I feel like I’m failing—at my job, at being a wife. I just want to feel like myself again, but I don’t know how.

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D018_m026.question:
I’m 65, been working as a janitor in a big office building for nearly 20 years now. My wife and I have been married 42 years—she’s been telling me for months I need to talk to somebody. Ever since that night on the job, about a year and a half ago, when I found that man after… after he’d taken his own life in one of the restrooms—I haven’t been the same. 

I can’t go near that floor without my chest tightening up. I asked my boss to reassign my route—said I’d take any other floor, just not that one. Even the smell of disinfectant in the men’s room makes me shaky. I avoid the break room now too, ’cause sometimes guys talk about it, not knowing it was me who found him. 

I keep thinking, *should’ve gotten there sooner… maybe said something… done something.* It wasn’t my fault, the police said so, but I still feel ashamed, like I failed. 

Sleep? I’m up every morning at 3 a.m., wide awake, heart racing. I lie there listening to the clock tick, too tired to move but too wired to rest. I don’t want my wife to worry, but I can’t keep living like this.
D018_m026.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m027.question:

The worst part is the feeling of being trapped in that moment, like I’m still seeing it happen and can’t move, can’t scream. That horror doesn’t fade—it’s constant.

I sleep, maybe seven hours most nights, but I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t rest at all. My body feels heavy, wired at the same time. It’s been like this for over a year and a half. I thought I’d adapt, but it’s only gotten harder.
D018_m027.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m028.question:

D018_m028.options:

    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m029.question:

Sometimes, I’ll be in a meeting, and suddenly I’m back there: my chest tightens, I can’t hear clearly, like the world’s muffled. I freeze. People have to call my name twice.

I don’t talk about it. I push it down. If I start thinking about that night, I get this wave of panic, like I’m drowning. So I just don’t go there. I avoid walking past buildings under construction, anything with that burnt wiring smell. My apartment? I keep it lit at night, even if I’m exhausted.

Sleep’s been hell. I wake up drenched, heart racing, maybe two or three times a night. Can’t get back under. I tell myself I don’t need rest—I’ve got a company to save. But… some mornings, I don’t know if I’m in the present or back in that hallway, smoke curling under the door. The fear hasn’t lessened. It’s like it’s frozen right there, clawing at me.
D018_m029.options:

    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m030.question:

I yell at the TV, punched a hole in the wall last winter when the heater clicked. I feel like I’m still at war—only now, there’s nobody to fight but myself. I can’t keep living like this, doctor. I just… don’t know how not to.

I ain’t been the same at work either. Used to take pride in finishing what I started, now I’ll show up, stare at a wall, and can’t even pick up the tools. Feels pointless, like nothing matters. The world just feels broken—dangerous, cold. I don’t know how much longer I can keep going like this.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D018_m046.question:

I used to get excited about little things, a good coffee, a sunny day. Now? Nothing lands.

D018_m047.question:

D018_m048.question:
I’ve been struggling for almost two years now—since the accident. I was driving home from an early-morning session with a client when a truck ran a red light and hit me head-on. I got lucky, physically. Some broken ribs, a concussion, but I healed. But my nerves… they never settled.

Sometimes, just hearing a car door slam loud or the screech of tires—it hits me like a punch in the gut. My heart races, my palms sweat, like I’m back there, trapped in that twisted metal. I can’t go near that intersection. I’ve rerouted all my morning sessions. I even avoid driving with my friend who was in the passenger seat—he didn’t make it—and that guilt claws at me every day.

Lately, things I used to love—helping clients hit PRs, hanging out at the gym after class, even going to the beach—feel hollow. I smile, but it doesn’t reach me. No real joy. I thought it’d pass, but it’s only gotten worse.

And now? If someone taps my shoulder from behind, I flinch so hard I’ve startled them. Not like me—I used to be the calm one, the steady presence. Now I feel on edge all the time, like danger’s just around the corner. It’s messing with my work, my sleep… everything.

D018_m050.question:
